CHIEF COMPLAINT
Positive hepatitis C lab work found on routine physical screening.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports feeling fine and is surprised by positive hepatitis C antibody test result obtained as part of routine physical. Denies prior diagnosis of hepatitis C. Has history of intravenous drug use but has been clean for over 15 years. Currently drinks beer occasionally, approximately one per day, decreased from previous use. Smokes one to two cigarettes per day, reports difficulty quitting. Concerned about potential transmission to wife and children.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No other medical conditions reported. Recent physical examination was otherwise unremarkable.

MEDICATIONS
Not taking any medications.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY
History of intravenous drug use, clean for over 15 years. Current alcohol use: one beer per day. Current tobacco use: one to two cigarettes per day. Married with children.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: No distress, no jaundice. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm with grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Lungs: Clear without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: Bowel sounds present, soft, no splenomegaly. Musculoskeletal: No gait disturbance or edema. Vitals reviewed and within normal limits.

RESULTS
HCV antibody: Positive. Liver panel: AST elevated at 39, ALT within normal limits, albumin within normal limits, total bilirubin within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C infection confirmed by positive HCV antibody. Plan to confirm diagnosis with additional testing including HCV RNA and HCV genotype. Ultrasound elastography ordered to assess for liver fibrosis and determine severity of liver disease. Family screening recommended with HCV antibody test; will assist with setting up appointments with family doctor. Follow-up appointment in three weeks to review results and determine treatment plan as needed. Nursing staff to provide orders prior to discharge.
